note: this cannot be judged as written: no price is shown on a part's row at all - not even for someone who is allowed to see financial data - so there is nothing to watch being hidden. The rule underneath it IS working, measured a different way.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39.

WHAT THE CHECK ASKS: with financial access the part's row shows its real price; without it, the same row appears with the price hidden.

WHAT HAPPENS: typing ZZTOGPRICE returns the part ZZTOGPRICE Filter both times, and the row reads the same both times - 'ZZTOGPRICE Filter, 9 Available, ZZTOGPRICE-1002'. NO PRICE IS SHOWN EITHER WAY. So the first half of the check cannot be demonstrated, and a price-less row must not be read as a clean hiding of the price.

THE RULE ITSELF IS WORKING, measured in the data the screen is built from: for the person WITH financial access the part's price of 137.45 is included; for the person WITHOUT it the price is not sent at all. So the permission does mask the price - it is only the row on screen that never showed one.

WHY THIS IS NOT A FAULT AGAINST THE PRODUCT: the requirements list what a part's row displays - its description, its part number, and the quantity with its stock badge. A price is not one of them. Prices are specified for part-sale rows, and purchase-order rows do show one on screen today.

What needs to be done: permission to correct this check so it watches a record whose row is meant to show a price - a purchase order shows one today. The masking rule itself needs no work.

note: this cannot be set up on this build: permissions here grant or deny a whole TYPE of record, never one particular record, so there is no way to make a person see some work orders but not one of them.
evidence:
Run on 20 September 2026, build v26.36.8-d146c39.

WHAT THE CHECK NEEDS: a role that can see SOME records of a type and is blocked from at least one specific record of that same type, so that the count on the heading can be compared against what the person may see.

WHAT THIS BUILD OFFERS: every permission measured in this pass grants or denies an entire type - parts, work orders, customers, part sales, supplier ordering, financial data. When one is removed the whole heading disappears; nothing hides a single record while leaving its neighbours visible.

WHY IT IS NOT RECORDED AS A PASS: the check asserts that a hidden record is not counted. If no record can be hidden, the check passes without proving anything - which is worse than recording it honestly as not testable here.

What needs to be done: a decision from the Product Owner on whether record-level access is meant to exist at all. Until then this stays not available on this build.
